findings.source: RequestBody TemplateDTO.template, arbitrary JSON string. No @Valid, whitelist, pattern, length check or escaping. The optional applicationInstId does not gate template evaluation.
findings.sink: <org.hzero.boot.interfaces.helper.FreeMarkerHelper: java.lang.Object invokeTemplate(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.Object[])> -> <groovy.lang.GroovyClassLoader: java.lang.Class parseClass(java.lang.String)> -> Class.newInstance() -> GroovyObject.invokeMethod(String,Object). Method names invoked include mockRequestPayloadDTO, mockResponsePayloadDTO, requestDataConverter and responseDataConverter. No CompilerConfiguration/SandboxTransformer.
findings.reason: The controller passes template.getTemplate() directly to ApplicationInstServiceImpl.testParamReflect, which calls FreeMarkerHelper.invokeTemplate(template, ...) before any use of the optional ID. FreeMarkerHelper compiles the same string with GroovyClassLoader.parseClass, instantiates the class, and invokes attacker-selected-by-code method names. The endpoint is an organization-level (and a duplicate site-level) API, not permissionWithin. Therefore an authenticated caller with the required tenant/site API permission can submit a Groovy class/script defining a called method and execute arbitrary Groovy/Java. Groovy 3.0.6 is packaged in srm-basic-interface-op.jar. The outer catch only converts exceptions to a failure DTO; it does not prevent side effects already executed.

findings.source: RequestBody TemplateDTO.template, arbitrary JSON string. interfaceId is optional and is not required before the template is compiled and invoked.
findings.sink: <org.hzero.boot.interfaces.helper.FreeMarkerHelper: java.lang.Object invokeTemplate(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.lang.Object[])> -> <groovy.lang.GroovyClassLoader: java.lang.Class parseClass(java.lang.String)> -> Class.newInstance() -> GroovyObject.invokeMethod(String,Object), followed by debugTemplateInvoke with requestDataConverter/responseDataConverter.
findings.reason: InterfaceController.debugParamTemplate and InterfaceSiteController.debugParamTemplate accept the template string from the HTTP body and pass it to InterfaceServiceImpl.debugParamTemplate. That method calls FreeMarkerHelper.invokeTemplate(template.getTemplate(), ...) and then debugTemplateInvoke, all without a validation, whitelist or sandbox. As with the application-instance endpoint, the first Groovy class compilation/instantiation is reached before any database lookup result is needed. Any authenticated organization-level or site-level user able to reach this interface-management API can execute Groovy code in the service JVM.

findings.entry: POST /v1/rule-engine/run-script (RuleEngineController#runGroovyScript; present in multiple service JARs including srm-gateway-op)
findings.source: RequestBody RuleEngine.script (String) and RuleEngine.params (Map), both JSON-controlled if the service endpoint is directly reachable.
findings.sink: <groovy.lang.GroovyShell: groovy.lang.Script parse(java.lang.String)> at RuleEngineServiceImpl:86, followed by Script.run() at line 87.
findings.reason: The method does compile attacker-controlled script with GroovyShell and only installs two GroovyInterceptors: NoSystemExitSandbox blocks System.exit and NoRunTimeSandbox blocks static calls on Runtime. That sandbox is incomplete and would likely allow other execution primitives such as ProcessBuilder if the endpoint were reachable. However the controller is annotated @Permission(permissionWithin = true); the gateway GetPermissionFilter explicitly rejects any permission whose within flag is true with PERMISSION_WITH_IN before forwarding. Therefore this is not an external gateway route. It may still be exploitable by an attacker with direct access to a service port or an internal SSRF primitive, but that is outside the confirmed external HTTP entry path.
missing_evidence: Whether any service port exposing /v1/rule-engine/run-script is reachable from an attacker-controlled network position was not verified.
Whether another external endpoint can be used as an SSRF pivot to this within-only endpoint was not established.
The gateway helper version and route data in the live deployment may differ from the extracted JAR.

The scanner's zero Groovy result and the diagnose 'unknown' result are not treated as proof of absence.
